text:
mina (ACME SRE): hey team, heads up — after we rolled a flannel NetworkPolicy in prod, our Redwood Private agent pods stopped registering with the control plane. All agent pods are CrashLoopBackOff and logs show TLS handshake timeouts to controlplane.redwood-inference.com:443. customer impact: inference traffic failing.

bryan (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the agent logs and the NetworkPolicy you applied? also, do you see DNS resolution working from the agent pod?

mina (ACME SRE): here's a trimmed agent log from one pod: 
```
2026-03-17T10:12:14Z ERROR agent: registration failed: handshake timeout
2026-03-17T10:12:14Z WARN  agent: retrying registration in 10s
2026-03-17T10:12:24Z ERROR agent: tls: failed to verify certificate: remote error: tls: handshake failure
```
and when I exec into the pod: 
```
# dig controlplane.redwood-inference.com @10.96.0.10 +timeout=2
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
# curl -v https://controlplane.redwood-inference.com --max-time 5
* Connected to controlplane.redwood-inference.com (10.11.5.241) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* timed out
* Connection timed out after 5001 milliseconds
```
So DNS is flaky from the pod and TLS handshake doesn't complete.

bryan (Support): thanks — please also share the NetworkPolicy YAML. flannel + NetworkPolicy can be restrictive if you had a default-deny.

mina (ACME SRE): pasted NP we applied (redacted): 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress-prod
  namespace: redwood-agent
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12    # cluster pod/cidr
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```
This was meant to lock down egress but I think we accidentally blocked outbound 443 and DNS to external resolvers.

ek (Eng - Private): yep — that NP only allows UDP/53 to the cluster CIDR and nothing else. Redwood agent needs outbound TCP 443 to controlplane redwood hostnames (SNI is required for certificate validation), and UDP/TCP 53 to your DNS server (or access to an egress resolver). Flannel's NetworkPolicy enforces by IP/CIDR so we can't allow by FQDN there.

ek (Eng - Private): quick repro steps/support commands we usually ask customers to run from one of the agent pods (if you can):
```
# inside agent pod
# check DNS reachability
nc -vz -w3 10.96.0.10 53 || echo "dns udp connect failed"
dig +short controlplane.redwood-inference.com @10.96.0.10
# test TLS handshake directly to control plane IP
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername controlplane.redwood-inference.com -brief
# tcpdump to confirm packets/egress
tcpdump -n -i any host controlplane.redwood-inference.com or port 53 -c 100
```
These will show whether packets leave the pod and whether DNS resolves.

bryan (Support): mitigation options in order of safety: 
1) Add an egress rule to the NetworkPolicy to allow TCP 443 to the controlplane IP(s) (or the NAT egress CIDR) and UDP/TCP 53 to your cluster DNS kube-dns service IP. Example patch below.
2) If you use a shared NAT egress IP, allow TCP 443 to that IP block so agents can reach the control plane hostnames through NAT.
3) As a temporary emergency, remove the NetworkPolicy to restore traffic while you craft a least-privileged policy.

bryan (Support): example NetworkPolicy egress snippet (you can kubectl apply -f -): 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-agent-egress
  namespace: redwood-agent
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12   # cluster DNS / kube-proxy if needed
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.11.5.241/32 # controlplane IP (replace with your resolved IP)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Note: replace the controlplane IP with the IP your DNS resolves. If controlplane is behind multiple IPs, add them or allow the NAT egress CIDR.

mina (ACME SRE): OK applying a narrow patch now to allow UDP 53 -> kube-dns svc (10.96.0.10) and TCP 443 -> controlplane IP returned by dig (10.11.5.241). Will report back.

deploy-bot: patch applied by mina at 2026-03-17T10:34:12Z (kubectl apply -f -) :white_check_mark:

mina (ACME SRE): patched and rolling, pods are now coming up and agents registered — looks good :tada: logs show successful TLS handshake. Thank you!

ek (Eng - Private): great. follow-up recommendations:
- If you can't allow IPs (dynamic control plane IPs), put agents in a namespace with an egress gateway/NAT that has a stable IP and allow that IP through your firewall.
- Consider an explicit NetworkPolicy that allows egress to your DNS service + control plane range and denies everything else.
- For long-term, we can provide a control-plane CIDR list and a small script to periodically resolve controlplane hostnames and reconcile NetworkPolicy objects if you want automation.

mina (ACME SRE): appreciate the guidance. I'll keep that automation idea in mind. Closing the escalation.

bryan (Support): closing on our side too — ping us if it recurs or if you want help generating the reconciler script. :thumbsup:
